items.q: Sectoral redness with mild irritation blanching fully with phenylephrine is what?
o: Episcleritis needing only lubricants or brief NSAIDs
items.exp: Superficial vessels constrict while deep scleral plexus stays engorged in true scleritis; episcleritis never threatens vision and recurs benignly. Nodular variants ache more but still blanch.
items.kp: Blanches white with drops: episclera only.

items.q: Deep boring eye pain waking the patient with violaceous non blanching redness suggests what?
o: Anterior scleritis needing systemic workup and therapy
items.exp: Severe tenderness with sleep disturbance marks scleral inflammation often tied to rheumatoid or vasculitis; topical steroids alone undertreat and perforation looms in necrotising forms.

items.q: Painless scleral thinning with bluish hue in longstanding rheumatoid hands is what?
o: Scleromalacia perforans needing protection and immunosuppression despite quiet eye
items.exp: Necrotising without inflammation melts silently toward perforation with trivial trauma; shields, lubrication and rheumatology escalation with tectonic graft cover defects. Redness absence misleads.
r: Incorrect. Episclera is red and benign.
items.kp: Quiet blue melt in rheumatoid: guard against perforation.

items.q: B scan T sign in a painful eye losing vision with choroidal folds indicates what?
o: Posterior scleritis with sub Tenon fluid
items.exp: Fluid outlining globe and optic nerve forms a T; systemic anti inflammatories rescue vision while masquerading tumours undergo needless enucleation without scans.
r: Incorrect. Detachment lacks T fluid pattern.
items.kp: T of fluid behind globe: posterior scleritis.

items.q: Scleritis workup must hunt which systemic associations?
o: Rheumatoid, ANCA vasculitis, tuberculosis, syphilis and gout
items.exp: Near half of scleritis ties to systemic disease; serologies, chest imaging and rheumatology input change survival in vasculitis beyond the eye. Infectious cases follow trauma or surgery separately.
r: Correct. Connective tissue and vasculitis hunt.
items.kp: Scleritis means body wide vasculitis hunt.

o: Perforated corneal ulcer healing with iris incarceration bulging
items.exp: Weak scar ectasia under pressure lines with uvea;tectonic grafting or evisceration pathways follow cosmesis and pain. Intercalary and ciliary variants follow limbal and ciliary injury.
r: Correct. Ulcer scar bulge with iris.
items.kp: Burst ulcer scar bulging with iris: staphyloma.

items.q: Child with blue sclera, repeated fractures and hearing loss most likely has what?
items.exp: Type I collagen defects blue the sclera, break bones and deafen (stapes); bisphosphonates, hearing aids and fracture care follow genetics. Non accidental injury lacks scleral and family pattern.
r: Incorrect. Sclera stays white in trauma.
items.kp: Blue eyes plus broken bones: brittle collagen.

items.q: Posterior staphyloma in pathological myopia threatens sight through what?
o: Macular degeneration, lacquer cracks and retinal detachment risk needing surveillance
items.exp: Ectatic posterior pole stretches retina into atrophy and holes; regular dilated exams with myopic maculopathy grading and detachment counselling preserve remaining vision.
items.kp: Long eye bulging behind: watch macula and retina.

items.q: Infectious scleritis after pterygium surgery with purulent nodule needs what?
o: Debridement with fortified antibiotics and organism hunt
items.exp: Pseudomonas and fungi seed bare sclera avascular beds; aggressive surgical sampling with intensive antimicrobials saves globe where steroids melt it. Rheumatology still excludes dual disease.
items.kp: Pus on bare sclera post surgery: debride and fortify.

items.q: Nodular versus diffuse anterior scleritis differ in which bedside feature?
o: Fixed deep tender nodule versus widespread violaceous engorgement
items.exp: Nodules fix to sclera resisting cotton bud movement unlike episcleritis; both ache deeply and need systemic therapy, nodular disease often heralding rheumatoid nodules elsewhere.
items.kp: Fixed deep nodule aching: nodular scleritis.
